svg.text: Nearby Friends — High-Fanout Real-Time Location Architecture (10M Concurrent · 333.3k Writes/s · 13.33M Pushes/s)
Stateful WebSocket Gateways · 10-Min TTL Valkey Location Cache · 134–140 CPU-Bound Sharded Pub/Sub Nodes · Cassandra History
1. Mobile Clients & Edge LB
Active Mobile User (Sender)
• 10M concurrent active users
• Sends GPS frame every 30 s
WS: { lat, lon, ts }
• Receives nearby friends <= 5 mi
L4/L7 Load Balancer
• Routes bidirectional stateful
WebSocket connections
• Routes HTTP REST friend/auth
calls to stateless API Fleet
• Graceful connection draining
Online Friend Clients (40 avg)
• 400 avg friends x 10% online
= 40 active subscribers/user
Receive update ONLY if:
1. Haversine dist <= 5 miles, OR
2. Friend just exited 5-mi radius
2. Stateful WebSocket Gateways & Auxiliary REST Tier
Stateful WebSocket Server Fleet (Connection & Distance Engine)
A. On Client Connect (Initialization Handshake):
1. Fetch user's 400 friend_ids from User Database / API
2. Pipelined MGET friend locations from TTL Location Cache
3. Filter Haversine <= 5 miles (8,046.72 m) & seed client map
4. SSUBSCRIBE to all 400 friend channels on Pub/Sub Ring
B. On 30s Periodic GPS Frame from Connected User:
1. Async append (user_id, lat, lon, ts) to Cassandra History
2. SETEX user_id 600 {lat, lon, ts} in Valkey Location Cache
3. Update local WS in-memory coord map + SPUBLISH user_ch:{id}
C. On Receiving Friend Update from Subscribed Pub/Sub Channel:
1. Compare friend (lat, lon) against local user's RAM coords
2. Push quantized distance bucket if <= 5 mi (or LEFT_RADIUS)
3. Anti-stalking: 0.5-mi buckets block 3-circle trilateration!
Stateless REST API Servers + User / Friendship DB
• Handles auth, profile management, and add/remove friend mutations
• User DB sharded by user_id (caps whale accounts at 5,000 friends)
• On Add/Remove Friend callback: notifies owning WS server to
dynamically SSUBSCRIBE or SUNSUBSCRIBE friend's channel
3. Sharded Pub/Sub Ring, TTL Cache & History Storage
Valkey / Redis Sharded Pub/Sub Cluster (134–140 CPU-Bound Nodes)
1 channel per user: "user_ch:{user_id}" (100M pre-allocated)
• Memory math: 100M channels + 400M subscriber ptrs = ~200 GB RAM
(Fits on 2 x 100 GB servers by RAM, but CPU-bound by fan-out!)
• Fan-out CPU math: 333.3k writes/s x 40 online friends
= 13.33M (~14M) pushes/s @ 100k pushes/s/node -> 134–140 nodes!
• Routed via etcd/ZK Consistent Hash Ring or Valkey SPUBLISH
Ephemeral Location Cache (Sharded Valkey with 10-Min TTL)
Key: "loc:{user_id}" -> Value: { lat, lon, ts } (TTL = 600 s)
• 10M active users x ~100 B = ~1.0 GB total active working set
• Sharded across 10–16 nodes to absorb 333.3k SETEX writes/s
• Auto-evicts users offline > 10 min with zero background cron
Location History DB (Apache Cassandra / ScyllaDB LSM Cluster)
PRIMARY KEY ((user_id, day_bucket), timestamp DESC)
• Absorbs 333.3k append-only LSM writes/s (~28.8B rows/day)
• Decoupled from real-time friend fan-out via async Kafka/workers
• Feeds ML trip analytics, fraud detection, and safety audits
4. Critical Staff Deep Dives: The Redis Cluster Broadcast Trap, Ring Resharding & Geohash Random Discovery
The Redis Cluster Legacy PUBLISH Broadcast Trap
Legacy PUBLISH user_ch:42 (Pre-Redis 7.0 Cluster):
• Broadcasts every message across the internal cluster
bus to ALL 140 nodes (333.3k x 140 = 46.7M msgs/s!)
• Every node burns 100% CPU parsing irrelevant publishes
Fix A: Valkey / Redis 7.0+ Sharded Pub/Sub (SPUBLISH)
Scopes channel strictly to its hash-slot owner (0 bus spam)
Fix B: Standalone shards + etcd Consistent Hash Ring
Pub/Sub Ring Resharding & Resubscription Storms
• Stateful channels require WS servers to tear down old
subscriptions and issue new SSUBSCRIBE commands on scale
Naive hash(ch) % N: Moves ~99% of channels on +1 node!
Consistent Hash Ring (150 vnodes) in etcd / ZooKeeper:
• Relocates only ~1/(N+1) (< 1% at N=140) of channels
• Schedule planned resharding at 03:00 diurnal traffic
trough + overprovision 20-30% CPU headroom
"Nearby Random Person" & Erlang/BEAM Alternative
Random Discovery: Geohash Pub/Sub Pool (geohash_ch:{L5})
• Opt-in user publishes to their current Geohash-5 cell
• Subscribes to CENTER + 8 NEIGHBOR cells (9 channels)
so strangers across a cell border are never missed!
Erlang / Elixir (BEAM / Phoenix PubSub) Alternative:
• Models each user as a ~300-word (~2.4 KB) BEAM actor; unifies
WS connections and distributed pub/sub without Redis tier
